the heterotrophic respiration is a passive ecosystem cooling process, which is affected by shading and temperature, and that the heterotrophs are not able to utilize the additional carbon from NPK-fertilizer in drained tropical peats.

peatland management and land-use changes can have large impacts on peat temperature and greenhouse gas emissions, and that the impacts are dependent on site characteristics, such as the peatland history, vegetation and hydrological conditions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature of tropical peatlands can be greatly affected by shading, and the temperature change affects the magnitude and direction of greenhouse gas dynamics.
the temperature response of peat heterotrophic respiration can be used for estimating CO2 effluxes from tropical peatlands.
the peat temperature dynamics and CO2 fluxes can be controlled by vegetation management and that the peat temperatures and CO2 flux responses can be expected to be site-specific.
